evidence: Lewis & Short: “inactive, lazy … without spirit, cowardly” (freq. and class.)
Plaut. Ep. 3.1.12: vae tibi, mūricīde homō (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A comic term of abuse. Traupman gives it as an adjective, mūricidus -a -um, chicken-hearted; Lewis & Short has the noun with a long second i.

sources: Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 290.
